properties.confidence_note: Citizens data public; depopulation program documented; ProPublica investigation on arbitration
properties.insurer_exits: Dozen+ carriers insolvent post-hurricanes Laura, Delta, Ida, Zeta (2020-2022). Citizens became largest insurer in state at 1.41M policies.
properties.regulatory_response: Aggressive depopulation program: 677,920 policies transferred to private market since Jan 2024. Citizens down from 1.41M to 395K policies.
properties.mortgage_impact: Coastal property values under pressure. Insurance costs now material factor in home affordability. Citizens wins 90%+ of arbitration cases it helps fund.
properties.one_line: Citizens went from 1.41M policies to 395K via forced depopulation — the state transferred risk back to a market that had already fled.

properties.confidence_note: FAIR Plan statistics public; State Farm nonrenewal data available; CDI press releases detailed
properties.insurer_exits: State Farm stopped new policies (2023), nonrenewing 72,000. Allstate, Farmers retreated. FAIR Plan up 139% since Sept 2021. 14% of FAIR policies now in lower-fire-risk urban zones — retreat beyond wildfire areas.
properties.regulatory_response: 25 moratorium declarations. SB 824 (2018) prohibits fire-risk nonrenewals. 9 new consumer protection laws effective 2026. 'Sustainable insurance strategy' trades rate hikes for writing commitments.
properties.mortgage_impact: Orinda ZIP 94563: 55% of homeowner policies nonrenewed by State Farm. LA fire zones (Brentwood, Beverly Hills) saw largest FAIR Plan growth. 26% of ZIP codes with $100M+ exposure growth.
properties.one_line: FAIR Plan up 139% in 4 years, now expanding beyond wildfire zones into normal urban areas — the retreat has its own momentum.

properties.confidence_note: TWIA annual reports public; deficit and exposure data detailed; rate inadequacy documented
properties.insurer_exits: Private insurers exiting coastal market. TWIA market share >50% in designated catastrophe areas. 276,000+ policies (record), projected 285,000 by end 2025.
properties.regulatory_response: TWIA entered 2025 with $413.5M deficit (reversed from $45.9M surplus). Residential rates deemed inadequate by 38%. Hurricane Beryl (July 2024) drained Catastrophe Reserve Trust Fund.
properties.mortgage_impact: Total TWIA exposure: $117B+ (record). Written premiums $779M projected 2025. Rising reinsurance costs and construction inflation compounding.
properties.one_line: TWIA holds $117B in coastal exposure with a $413M deficit — the insurer of last resort is itself underinsured.

properties.confidence_note: Post-hurricane insolvency wave documented; regulatory changes tracked; rate data available
properties.insurer_exits: Dozen+ carriers insolvent after Hurricanes Laura, Delta, Ida, Zeta. Many others stopped writing in high-risk areas. Highest rate increase in nation: 58%.
properties.regulatory_response: Repealed three-year protection rule (Jan 2025). Now allows up to 5% annual cancellations per insurer. Described as shift to 'business-friendly' climate — regulators chose market access over consumer protection.
properties.mortgage_impact: Highest rates in nation. Coastal communities face compounding exposure: hurricane risk + insurer exit + regulatory deprotection.
properties.one_line: Dozen+ insurers went insolvent, then the state repealed consumer protections to attract replacements — 58% rate increase followed.

properties.confidence_note: Marshall Fire data well-documented; insurance gap data from Boulder Reporting Lab; Xcel settlement public
properties.insurer_exits: Not primarily an exit story — Colorado is the underinsurance story. 1,105 homes destroyed in Marshall Fire (2021). Insurance gaps averaged >$100K per household. 87% had extended coverage but 75% still fell short.
properties.regulatory_response: Colorado Housing Recovery Program grants stopped new applications July 2024. Community Foundation rebuild fund running out (<$5M remaining). Xcel Energy + telecoms settled for $640M.
properties.mortgage_impact: Highest cumulative rate increase in nation: 76.6% over 6 years (2019-2024). Underinsured households significantly less likely to rebuild. Recovery funds expiring one by one.
properties.one_line: 87% of Marshall Fire victims had extended coverage — 75% still fell short. The coverage people thought they had was a fiction.

properties.confidence_note: Wind Pool data less publicly detailed than FL/TX; coastal exposure documented but granularity limited
properties.insurer_exits: Private carriers reducing coastal exposure. Wind Pool absorbing increasing share of coastal risk. Hurricane season exposure compounding with development pressure on barrier islands.
properties.regulatory_response: Rate regulation remains commonplace. Coastal building codes updated post-hurricanes. But development pressure on barrier islands continues largely unchecked.
properties.mortgage_impact: Outer Banks and coastal communities face rising premiums and shrinking coverage options. Flood insurance (NFIP) costs rising separately. Compound exposure: wind + flood + sea level.
properties.one_line: Barrier island development continues while insurers retreat — the state is building into exposure it's simultaneously losing coverage for.
